question: The terms = Dribbling, passing, shooting are associated with which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Basketball.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dribbling, passing and shooting are the three fundamental skills of Basketball. (बास्केटबॉल)

• Basketball was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 at Springfield, Massachusetts, USA.

• A basketball team has 5 players on court; the governing body is FIBA (founded 1932, HQ — Mies, Switzerland).

• Other basketball terms: slam dunk, rebound, layup, travelling, blocking, pivot, free throw.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shooting — a target sport; terms: bull's eye, trigger, range, air rifle, pistol.

• Badminton — terms: smash, drop shot, deuce, shuttle, love, let, drive.

• Cricket — terms: googly, LBW, maiden over, stumped, silly point, duck, no ball.

NOTE

• Basketball court size: 28 m × 15 m; basket height 10 feet (3.05 m).

• India's basketball body is the Basketball Federation of India (BFI), formed in 1950.

question: India's total length of coastline of the mainland including Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7516.6 km.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The total length of India's coastline, including the mainland, Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep Islands, is 7,516.6 km. (समुद्र तट रेखा)

• The mainland coastline alone measures about 6,100 km.

• Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states (about 1,600 km), followed by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's total land frontier (land boundary) is about 15,200 km.

• India's total geographical area is 32,87,263 sq km, about 2.4% of the world's land area.

• Nine states and four Union Territories lie along the Indian coast.

NOTE

• India's north–south extent is 3,214 km and east–west extent is 2,933 km.

• The Tropic of Cancer (23°30′N) passes through 8 Indian states; the standard meridian is 82°30′E passing through Mirzapur (UP).

question: The grading system used by the Mughals to fix rank, salary and military responsibilities is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mansabdari system.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar in 1571 (c. 1570s) to fix the rank, salary and military obligations of nobles. (मनसबदारी प्रणाली)

• Each mansabdar held a dual rank — Zat (personal status/salary) and Sawar (number of cavalrymen to be maintained).

• Mansabs ranged from 10 to 10,000; ranks above 5,000 were normally reserved for princes of the royal blood.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Iqta system — land-revenue assignment system of the Delhi Sultanate, introduced by Iltutmish.

• Ryotwari system — British land revenue settlement made directly with the ryot (cultivator), introduced by Thomas Munro/Alexander Read in Madras and Bombay.

• Mahalwari system — revenue settled with the village/mahal as a unit, introduced by Holt Mackenzie (1822) in North-Western Provinces.

NOTE

• Permanent Settlement (1793) — introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha with zamindars as landowners.

• Akbar's revenue system Dahsala/Zabti was implemented by his finance minister Raja Todar Mal.

question: Mallika Sarabhai was awarded with Padma Bhushan (2010) - for contribution to Performing Arts. She was highly recognized for which dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mallika Sarabhai is an eminent Indian dancer and activist trained in Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam. (कुचिपुड़ी और भरतनाट्यम)

• She received the Padma Bhushan in 2010 for her contribution to the performing arts.

• She is the daughter of the classical dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai and space scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, and directs the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts, Ahmedabad.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi — classical dance of Andhra Pradesh; exponents: Raja and Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Vempati Chinna Satyam.

• Bharatanatyam — classical dance of Tamil Nadu; exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy.

• Odissi — Odisha (Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh); Manipuri — Manipur (Jhaveri sisters); Kathakali — Kerala (Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair).

NOTE

• India's eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya.

• All classical dances derive from Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra.

question: Which of the following dance is particular to the women of the Kamad tribe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Terataal dance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Terataal (Terah Taali) is performed by the women of the Kamad tribe of Rajasthan. (तेरह ताली नृत्य)

• The dancers sit on the floor and strike thirteen manjiras (small brass cymbals) tied to different parts of the body, hence the name *Terah Taali*.

• It is performed in devotion to the folk deity Baba Ramdev (Ramdeoji), usually at Ramdevra.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bhutia dance — associated with the Bhutia community of Sikkim.

• Mask dance (Chham) — a Buddhist monastic dance of Sikkim, Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh.

• Garai/Garia dance — a tribal dance of Tripura performed during the Garia Puja.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan: Ghoomar, Kalbeliya, Kachhi Ghodi, Chari, Bhavai, Gair.

• Kalbeliya dance of Rajasthan was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

question: What is the currency of Bangladesh, a neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The currency of Bangladesh is the Taka (BDT). (टका)

• Its capital is Dhaka, and the central bank is the Bangladesh Bank.

• Bangladesh shares the longest land border with India (about 4,096 km), touching West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Yuan (Renminbi) — currency of China; capital Beijing.

• Ngultrum — currency of Bhutan; capital Thimphu.

• Kyat — currency of Myanmar; capital Nay Pyi Taw.

NOTE

• Neighbour currencies: Nepal — Nepalese Rupee; Sri Lanka — Sri Lankan Rupee; Pakistan — Pakistani Rupee; Maldives — Rufiyaa; Afghanistan — Afghani.

• India shares land borders with 7 countries — Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan.

question: The concept of "Amendment of the Constitution" in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South Africa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The procedure for amendment of the Constitution and the election of members of the Rajya Sabha were borrowed from the Constitution of South Africa. (संविधान संशोधन की प्रक्रिया)

• Amendment of the Indian Constitution is governed by Article 368 in Part XX.

• The Indian Constitution provides a blend of rigidity and flexibility — amendments by simple majority, special majority, and special majority plus ratification by half the states.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Germany (Weimar) — suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency.

• Canada — federation with a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Centre, appointment of Governors by the Centre.

• Australia — Concurrent List, freedom of trade and commerce, joint sitting of the two Houses.

NOTE

• Britain — parliamentary government, rule of law, single citizenship, writs.

• USA — Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independent judiciary, impeachment of the President, preamble.

• Ireland — DPSP, nomination to Rajya Sabha, method of election of the President; USSR — Fundamental Duties.

question: The Gram Sabha is a meeting of all adults who live in the area covered by a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is panchayat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gram Sabha is the body consisting of all registered voters (adults) in the area of a Gram Panchayat. (ग्राम सभा)

• It is defined in Article 243(b) of the Constitution and is the permanent, foundational unit of the Panchayati Raj system.

• The Gram Sabha approves the panchayat's budget and plans, reviews accounts, and selects beneficiaries of welfare schemes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Panchayati Raj was introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (in force from 24 April 1993), adding Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects).

• Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated at Nagaur, Rajasthan on 2 October 1959 by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, on the recommendation of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957).

• The 74th Amendment Act, 1992 deals with urban local bodies (Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule, 18 subjects).

NOTE

• Panchayati Raj is a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block), Zila Parishad (district).

• Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a two-tier system; L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) recommended constitutional status for panchayats.

question: As of 2022, who is the India's last living Sadhir dancer honoured with Padma Shri Award in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is R Muthukannammal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• R. Muthukannammal of Viralimalai, Tamil Nadu, is regarded as India's last living Sadhir (Devadasi) dancer and was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for Art. (सादिर नृत्य)

• Sadhir Attam is the older temple-dance tradition of the devadasis from which the modern classical form Bharatanatyam evolved.

• She was initiated into the temple dance tradition as a child and later taught the art to preserve it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rukmini Devi Arundale — revived and popularised Bharatanatyam and founded Kalakshetra (Chennai, 1936); Padma Bhushan 1956.

• Manjamma Jogati (B. Manjamma Jogati) — transgender folk dancer of the Jogati Nritya of Karnataka; Padma Shri 2021.

• Baisali Mohanty — an Odissi dancer.

NOTE

• Padma Awards order of precedence: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.

• Padma Awards were instituted in 1954 and are announced on Republic Day (26 January).

question: Which freedom fighter of British India is widely regarded as the "father of the two-nation theory"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Syed Ahmed Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (1817–1898) is widely regarded as the father/originator of the Two-Nation Theory, holding that Hindus and Muslims formed two distinct nations. (द्वि-राष्ट्र सिद्धांत)

• He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875, which became Aligarh Muslim University (1920).

• He started the Aligarh Movement for modern, Western education among Muslims and founded the journal Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Muhammad Ali Jinnah — later championed and politically implemented the two-nation theory; passed the Lahore/Pakistan Resolution (1940) and became the first Governor-General of Pakistan.

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak — 'Father of Indian Unrest'; slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"; started Ganapati and Shivaji festivals; papers Kesari and Maratha.

• Jawaharlal Nehru — first Prime Minister of India (1947–1964); author of *Discovery of India*.

NOTE

• The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dhaka by Nawab Salimullah and Aga Khan.

• Separate electorates for Muslims were granted by the Morley–Minto Reforms / Indian Councils Act, 1909.

question: Who presents the annual budget before the Lok Sabha?
option_3: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Union Finance Minister.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Union Budget (Annual Financial Statement) is presented in the Lok Sabha by the Union Finance Minister on behalf of the President. (वार्षिक वित्तीय विवरण)

• The Budget is mentioned in Article 112 of the Constitution as the Annual Financial Statement.

• A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and only on the recommendation of the President (Article 110); the Rajya Sabha can retain it for a maximum of 14 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The CAG (Article 148) audits government accounts and is called the guardian of the public purse; he does not present the budget.

• India's first Union Budget was presented by R. K. Shanmukham Chetty on 26 November 1947.

• Morarji Desai presented the highest number of budgets (10).

NOTE

• Since 2017 the budget is presented on 1 February, and the Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget.

• Indira Gandhi was the first woman to present the Union Budget (1970); Nirmala Sitharaman is the first full-time woman Finance Minister to do so (2019).

question: Under which amendment act, article 51A (k) of the Indian constitution was inserted in the constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eighty – sixth amendment Act.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A(k) — the duty of a parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the ages of 6 and 14 years — was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. (मौलिक कर्तव्य)

• It is the 11th Fundamental Duty, the only one added after the original ten.

• The same 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A (Right to Education) as a Fundamental Right and modified Article 45.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• 82nd Amendment Act, 2000 — allowed relaxation in qualifying marks for reservation in promotion for SC/STs.

• 84th Amendment Act, 2001 — froze the readjustment of Lok Sabha/Assembly seats on the basis of the 1991 census till 2026.

• 81st Amendment Act, 2000 — provided for treating backlog vacancies of SC/ST as a separate class (carry forward rule).

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee; originally 10 duties.

• The RTE Act came into force on 1 April 2010.

question: In February 2022, Indian Government launched which operation to bring back Indians stranded in Ukraine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Operation Ganga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Operation Ganga was launched by the Government of India in February 2022 to evacuate Indian citizens, mostly students, stranded in Ukraine after the Russian invasion. (ऑपरेशन गंगा)

• Evacuation flights operated through neighbouring countries — Romania, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Moldova.

• Four Union Ministers were sent as Special Envoys to coordinate the evacuation; over 22,500 Indians were brought back.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Operation Flood (1970) — the world's largest dairy development programme, launched by the NDDB under Dr. Verghese Kurien, the 'Father of the White Revolution'.

• Operation Devi Shakti (2021) — evacuation of Indians from Afghanistan.

• Vande Bharat Mission (2020) — repatriation of Indians during the COVID-19 pandemic.

NOTE

• Operation Kaveri (2023) — evacuation of Indians from Sudan.

• Operation Rahat (2015) — evacuation from Yemen; Operation Maitri (2015) — relief in Nepal after the earthquake.

question: Which act was passed by the British Parliament to control the territories of the East India Company majorly in Bengal in the year 1773?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Regulating Act.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first step by the British Parliament to control and regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India. (रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट, 1773)

• It designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal — Lord Warren Hastings was the first — with an Executive Council of four members.

• It provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta (established 1774) with one Chief Justice and three other judges, and made the Bombay and Madras Presidencies subordinate to Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Charter Acts were passed in 1793, 1813, 1833 and 1853; the Charter Act of 1833 made Lord William Bentinck the first Governor-General of India.

• Indian Councils Acts — 1861, 1892, 1909 (Morley–Minto) — dealt with legislative councils and representation.

• Government of India Acts — 1858, 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford), 1935 — transferred power to the Crown and introduced dyarchy/provincial autonomy.

NOTE

• Pitt's India Act, 1784 established a Board of Control and a system of double government.

• The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly except in tea and trade with China.

question: Indian musician Ustad Alla Rakha Qureshi is associated with ___ musical instrument.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Alla Rakha Qureshi (1919–2000) was a legendary tabla maestro of the Punjab gharana. (तबला)

• He is best known for his accompaniment to Pandit Ravi Shankar on the sitar, taking Indian percussion to global audiences.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (1977) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1982); his son Ustad Zakir Hussain is also a world-famous tabla player.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Flute (Bansuri) — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pannalal Ghosh.

• Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, Buddhadev Das Gupta.

• Santoor — Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, Bhajan Sopori.

NOTE

• The tabla is a membranophone (avanaddha vadya); the sitar and sarod are string (tat vadya) instruments; the flute is a wind (sushir vadya) instrument.

• Other instrument-artist pairs: Sitar — Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan; Shehnai — Bismillah Khan; Sarangi — Ram Narayan; Veena — S. Balachander; Mridangam — Palghat Mani Iyer.

question: After the victory over Sakas, who among the following adopted the title of 'Vikramaditya'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chandragupta II (c. 380–415 CE) defeated the Saka (Western Kshatrapa) ruler Rudrasimha III and assumed the title 'Vikramaditya' (also 'Sakari' — destroyer of the Sakas). (विक्रमादित्य)

• His conquest of Gujarat, Kathiawar and Malwa gave the Guptas access to the western sea ports; he made Ujjain a second capital.

• The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during his reign; his court is traditionally associated with the Navaratna, including Kalidasa and Amarasimha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta I — first great Gupta ruler; took the title Maharajadhiraja and married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi.

• Samudragupta — called the 'Napoleon of India' by V.A. Smith; his exploits are recorded in the Allahabad (Prayag) Prashasti by Harisena.

• Skandagupta — repelled the Huna invasion; Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda University and took the title Mahendraditya.

NOTE

• The Gupta period (c. 319–550 CE) is called the Golden Age of India; the Gupta Era was started by Chandragupta I in 319–320 CE.

• The Mehrauli Iron Pillar at Delhi is associated with King Chandra, generally identified with Chandragupta II.

question: "Goitre" is a disease of which of the following glands?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thyroid gland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Goitre is the abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland, caused mainly by a deficiency of iodine in the diet. (घेंघा रोग)

• The thyroid secretes thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), which need iodine; it also secretes calcitonin, which lowers blood calcium.

• Goitre is prevented by using iodised salt; the thyroid is the largest endocrine gland in the human body.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pancreas — a mixed gland; insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus; it also secretes glucagon.

• Adrenal gland — secretes adrenaline (emergency hormone); its deficiency causes Addison's disease.

• Pituitary gland — the 'master gland'; excess growth hormone causes gigantism/acromegaly, deficiency causes dwarfism.

NOTE

• Hypothyroidism in children causes cretinism; in adults it causes myxoedema.

• Hyperthyroidism causes Grave's disease (exophthalmic goitre).

question: The materials, through which things can be seen, are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is transparent materials.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Materials through which things can be seen clearly are called transparent materials. (पारदर्शी पदार्थ)

• They allow almost all light to pass through without scattering — e.g. clear glass, water, air, cellophane.

• Transparency depends on how light is transmitted; transparent objects do not form a dark shadow of their own material.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Opaque materials — do not allow light to pass at all and form sharp shadows, e.g. wood, stone, metal, cardboard.

• Translucent materials — allow partial/diffused light to pass so objects are not clearly seen, e.g. butter paper, frosted glass, oiled paper.

• Conductive materials — allow heat or electricity to pass through, e.g. copper, aluminium; this is unrelated to light transmission.

NOTE

• Light travels in a straight line (rectilinear propagation); a shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light.

• The speed of light in vacuum is 3 × 10⁸ m/s; a luminous body emits its own light (sun), a non-luminous body does not (moon).

question: According to census 2011, what is the population (nearest value) of tribals in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.42 crore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, the Scheduled Tribe (tribal) population of India is about 10.43 crore (104 million), i.e. roughly 10.42 crore — about 8.6% of the total population. (अनुसूचित जनजाति)

• The Scheduled Caste population is about 20.14 crore, i.e. 16.6% of the total population.

• Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population; Mizoram has the highest percentage of STs (about 94.4%); Lakshadweep also has a very high ST share.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's total population in Census 2011 was 121.08 crore; the decadal growth rate was 17.7%.

• Article 342 empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes of a state or UT.

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th after Independence; its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

NOTE

• Census 2011 — sex ratio 943, literacy 74.04%, density 382 persons/sq km.

• Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest literacy — Kerala; lowest — Bihar.

question: Which of the following is an agro-based industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sugar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Agro-based industries use agricultural produce as raw material; the sugar industry uses sugarcane, so it is agro-based. (कृषि आधारित उद्योग)

• Other agro-based industries: cotton textiles, jute, silk, woollen textiles, vegetable oil, tea, coffee, paper (from bagasse), rubber.

• India is the second largest producer of sugarcane in the world after Brazil; Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are the leading sugar-producing states.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Aluminium and Iron and Steel are mineral-based industries — they use bauxite and iron ore respectively.

• Coal is a mineral/fossil fuel, not an agricultural product; it is the main raw material for thermal power and metallurgical coke.

• India's first modern sugar mill was set up at Betia, Bihar (1903).

NOTE

• Industry classification by raw material: agro-based, mineral-based, marine-based, forest-based.

• Major iron and steel plants: Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), Rourkela (Odisha), Durgapur (WB), Bokaro (Jharkhand), Bhadravati (Karnataka), Jamshedpur/TISCO (Jharkhand).

question: The upper portion of the mantle is called _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is asthenosphere.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The upper portion of the mantle is called the asthenosphere, extending to about 400 km depth. (दुर्बलतामंडल)

• It is the main source of magma that reaches the surface during volcanic eruptions, and its plastic, semi-molten nature allows the movement of tectonic plates.

• The mantle lies between the crust and the core, extending from about 100 km to 2,900 km, and constitutes about 84% of the Earth's volume.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lithosphere — the rigid outer shell comprising the crust and the uppermost solid mantle, about 10–200 km thick; it is broken into tectonic plates.

• Mesosphere — the lower mantle (in geology); in atmospheric science, the layer above the stratosphere where meteors burn up.

• Barysphere — a term used for the interior of the Earth beneath the lithosphere, sometimes for the core.

NOTE

• Earth's core (NiFe/barysphere) extends from 2,900 km to 6,371 km; the outer core is liquid and the inner core solid.

• Discontinuities: Mohorovicic (crust–mantle), Gutenberg (mantle–core), Lehmann (outer–inner core), Conrad (SIAL–SIMA).

question: Olympic Games 1952 were held in which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helsinki.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 1952 Summer Olympics (Games of the XV Olympiad) were held in Helsinki, Finland. (हेलसिंकी, फ़िनलैंड)

• The Soviet Union participated in the Olympics for the first time at these Games.

• India won a bronze medal in wrestling through K. D. Jadhav at Helsinki 1952 — India's first individual Olympic medal; India also won gold in hockey.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• London hosted the Olympics in 1908, 1948 and 2012.

• Berlin hosted the 1936 Olympics, where Jesse Owens won four gold medals.

• New York has never hosted the Olympic Games; the USA hosted them at St. Louis (1904), Los Angeles (1932, 1984) and Atlanta (1996).

NOTE

• The modern Olympics began at Athens in 1896; the IOC was founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin (HQ — Lausanne, Switzerland).

• Olympic motto: "Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter" (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together).

question: Snails is an example of which of the phylum of animal kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mollusca.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Snails belong to the phylum Mollusca, the second largest phylum of the animal kingdom. (मोलस्का संघ)

• Molluscs have a soft, unsegmented body, usually covered by a calcareous shell, with a muscular foot and a mantle; many possess a rasping organ called the radula.

• Examples: snail, slug, octopus, squid, oyster, mussel, Pila, Chiton.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Arthropoda — the largest phylum; jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton, e.g. cockroach, prawn, spider, butterfly.

• Annelida — metamerically segmented worms with a true coelom, e.g. earthworm, leech, Nereis.

• Protochordates — primitive chordates like Amphioxus (Branchiostoma), Herdmania, Balanoglossus.

NOTE

• Pearls are obtained from the oyster (Pinctada), a mollusc.

• Octopus is the most intelligent mollusc; the giant squid is the largest invertebrate.

question: The famous Pandav Leni Caves is located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pandav Leni (Pandavleni/Trirashmi) Caves are located near Nashik in Maharashtra. (पांडवलेणी गुफाएँ)

• They form a group of about 24 Buddhist (Hinayana) rock-cut caves carved between the 1st century BCE and the 3rd century CE.

• They contain important inscriptions of the Satavahana, Western Kshatrapa and Abhira rulers, including those of Gautamiputra Satakarni and Nahapana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other famous caves of Maharashtra: Ajanta, Ellora, Elephanta, Karla, Bhaja, Bedse, Kanheri.

• Odisha — Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves (Jain, of King Kharavela).

• Bihar — Barabar Caves, the oldest rock-cut caves, of the Mauryan period, granted to the Ajivikas by Ashoka.

NOTE

• Ajanta (paintings, Buddhist), Ellora (Buddhist, Hindu, Jain — Kailasa temple) and Elephanta (Shaivite, Trimurti) are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

• Nashik on the Godavari river is one of the four venues of the Kumbh Mela.

question: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio was a teacher of which college in 1820s?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindu college, Calcutta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Henry Louis Vivian Derozio (1809–1831) taught at Hindu College, Calcutta from 1826 to 1831. (हिंदू कॉलेज, कलकत्ता)

• He inspired the radical reformist movement called Young Bengal, and his followers were known as Derozians.

• He promoted free thinking, rationalism and questioning of social orthodoxy, and started the Academic Association; he died of cholera at the age of 22.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Hindu College was founded in 1817 by Raja Rammohan Roy, David Hare and Radhakanta Deb; it later became Presidency College (1855).

• Sanskrit College, Calcutta (1824) is associated with Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, who opened it to non-Brahmin students.

• Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore was founded in 1909 with the support of Jamsetji Tata.

NOTE

• Macaulay's Minute (1835) made English the medium of instruction; Wood's Despatch (1854) is called the Magna Carta of English education in India.

• Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were established in 1857.
